paper_title: Searching for Ultralight Dark Matter Conversion in Solar Corona using Low Frequency Array Data
coupling_convention: epsilon x (rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5, dimensionless kinetic mixing scaled by dark photon density fraction, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper sets 95% C.L. upper limits on dark photon kinetic mixing from resonant DPDM-to-photon conversion in the solar corona, using LOFAR solar observations (3x17 min in 2015). Text states the limit reaches ~1e-13 across the 30-80 MHz frequency range (mass 1.24e-7 to 3.31e-7 eV), roughly an order of magnitude better than CMB distortion bounds. Encoded as an approximately flat bound over the stated validity range since no numerical table is provided; the actual limit (Fig. 4) has zig-zag frequency structure varying around 1e-13 (roughly a few 1e-14 to a few 1e-13). The paper also derives an axion-photon coupling limit (~1e-9 to 1e-8 GeV^-1 range, Fig. 10), but it is subdominant to CAST and astrophysical bounds and carries large solar B-field uncertainty; the dark photon result is the primary limit.
